title: External Monitoring
markdown: `openexecutive.monitoring` watches the outside world on a heartbeat and turns detected changes into briefing proposals via the same alert pipeline that handles inbound email and Slack. The `external_monitor_scan` heartbeat (`__internal__` channel, default every 5 min) walks `list_watchlist(enabled_only=True)`, skipping rows fresher than their per-source cadence floor. For each due row it fires a read-only source adapter resolved from `_REGISTRY` by `signal_type`: - `vendor_status` — Statuspage Atom/RSS incident feeds (AWS, Stripe, GitHub, …). Reads each incident's current status out of the entry body, parses `` into `published_at`, and keys its dedup on `(entry id, )`; a **seeding** source (see below). - `rss` — generic Atom/RSS via feedparser (changelogs, layoffs.fyi, filings). Parses each entry's ``/`` into `published_at`; a **seeding** source (see below). - `stock` — Yahoo Finance chart endpoint; fires on `abs_change_pct_gte` moves. - `page_watch` — change-detection on a feed-less page. Fetches via the keyless httpx fetcher by default, or via xcrawl's scrape API when the row carries `config.fetch = "xcrawl"` — so JS-rendered / bot-blocked pages that publish no RSS (most modern news / marketing sites) are still monitorable. - `edgar` and the BILLED `query` web-search adapter. Each `Signal` is trigger-filtered, severity-clamped to the row's `[floor, ceiling]`, and INSERTed into `external_signals` where `UNIQUE(dedup_key)` drops replays. Survivors pass a suppression cascade (`baseline` → `stale` → `dry_run` → `below_floor` → capture-time relevance enrichment → promote), then `promote_signal_to_alert` builds an `AlertEvent` handed to `alerts.pipeline.schedule_evaluation` and surfaced as a `/today` proposal. Every signal carries two timestamps that are never conflated: `captured_at` (when the monitor first saw it) and `published_at` (when the upstream says it happened — RSS ``, EDGAR filing date; null for `stock`, `page_watch`, `query`). Two freshness gates run first in the cascade, before anything that costs an LLM call. **Baseline:** the first poll that returns entries for a row whose adapter declares `seed_on_first_poll` (`rss`, `edgar`) records every entry already in the feed — trigger misses included, so the first entry that ever matches a keyword is news and a later, wider trigger can't resurface old ones — as `suppressed_baseline`, promotes nothing, and stamps `watchlist.baselined_at`, so a new watch reports what changes from now on instead of replaying the feed's back-catalogue (the same idea as `page_watch`'s first-observation baseline). It is keyed on `baselined_at` rather than `last_polled_at`, so a failed first fetch can't forfeit it; the claim and the recording are one transaction (a compare-and-swap on the stamp plus the rows, all-or-nothing), so of two overlapping scans exactly one records the back-catalogue and a failure part-way leaves nothing behind to replay; the other scan promotes only entries dated after that stamp (undated entries count as baseline, since the feed controls the date; entries dated more than a few minutes past its own clock are deferred rather than recorded); and baseline rows don't count against `max_signals_per_scan`, so a large feed can't be half-baselined. `vendor_status` used to sit outside both gates for a structural reason: its dedup key was `sha256(slug, entry id)`, and an incident's id never changes across its updates, so any suppressed insert muted that incident for good. Keying on `(entry id, )` instead (issue #90) makes a suppression cost one *state* of an incident rather than the incident, so both gates now apply to vendor feeds too — and an incident moving Investigating → Resolved mints a new key and surfaces, while re-polling an unchanged feed still dedups. Because a history feed's archive is mostly incidents resolved months ago, the adapter also carves live news out of its own baseline: it reads each incident's current status from the entry body (Statuspage renders the newest update first as `Resolved` / `Investigating` / `Monitoring` / … — the body is parsed by a real HTML parser, off the event loop, and the reading is deliberately asymmetric: any sign that the incident is over closes it, wherever it appears, while only a marked-up label can say it is still open. Working out which update is newest turned out to be something tag soup cannot be trusted to express, and every attempt reported a long-resolved incident as live) and exempts the ones still OPEN via the optional `promote_on_baseline` hook, so a watch added during an outage reports that outage on its first poll while the resolved archive is recorded as `suppressed_baseline`. An unrecognised status counts as closed — a vendor changing feed format must not be able to promote its whole archive at HIGH, and nothing is lost, since the next `` bump surfaces normally. An exempt entry must still pass the row's trigger filter (one that misses stays in the baseline, so widening a trigger later cannot resurface it) and is still judged by the stale gate below: the exemption buys an entry past the baseline, never past its own timestamp, because "this is live" is a reading of vendor-controlled markup and an entry the feed dates outside the age window is not news whatever that reading says. **Stale:** a signal whose `published_at` is older than `EXTERNAL_MONITOR_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_DAYS` (default 7; `0` disables) at capture time is recorded as `suppressed_stale` and never promoted — a January article a feed resurfaces in September is not September news. An entry dated more than `EXTERNAL_MONITOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_HOURS` ahead (default 24; `0` disables; `config_json.max_future_skew_hours` overrides it per row for calendar or maintenance feeds that legitimately date entries ahead) is deferred instead: skipped for the tick and not recorded (recording would burn its dedup key and let a feed mute an announcement for good by post-dating it), with one aggregated `external_signal_deferred` audit row per poll — carrying each held-back entry's summary and link, and emitted even if the poll later raises — then judged normally once the date passes. Inside the window, the alert body handed to triage carries `Published:` and `Discovered:` lines so the item is judged on when it happened. Adapters prefer a plausible date key over one more than a day in the future (and keep the future value when every key is implausible, so the pipeline defers it rather than waving an undated entry through), and the alert body collapses whitespace in the summary so no source can forge its own labeled body line. The `query` adapter is a special case: it emits every web hit flat-LOW (it can't judge materiality per-hit), so for query signals enrichment runs BEFORE the floor gate and `_grade_query_severity` regrades from the relevance read (≥0.8 HIGH, ≥0.5 MEDIUM, else LOW). Without this, any query watch item with a `severity_floor` above LOW would suppress every hit — which is what left the Monitoring section empty even while standing queries were returning material findings. Which lane a proposal lands in is decided by `briefing.ranking.categorize`: an unrouted, low/medium signal from a monitoring source (`stock`, `vendor_status`, `rss`, `query`, `edgar`, `page_watch`, or any `external:*` topic tag) is `monitoring` (the collapsible Monitoring section); a routed or high/urgent one is `action` (the "Needs you" queue). The triage prompt's External Signals rule covers all six source kinds so it trusts the source and emits the `external:*` tags that drive this split. The watchlist is editable from chat (`add_watchlist_entry`, `tune_watchlist_entry`) and HTTP (`/watchlist`); the `executive_research` workflow proposes what to watch. Because that workflow is LLM-driven and historically proposed feed URLs it never verified (most were dead — 404 / 403 / not-actually-a-feed), every `rss` target is validated at insert time (`monitoring.target_validation`): a URL that fetches and parses as a feed is kept; a public page that isn't a feed is converted to a scrape-backed `page_watch` when xcrawl can read it, otherwise rejected (HTTP 422 / tool error); SSRF-blocked or unparseable URLs are rejected outright and never handed to xcrawl. Non-`rss` types insert unchanged with no network I/O. ### Invariants - Adapters are read-only — they never write upstream and never auto-execute. - Every `Signal` carries a deterministic `dedup_key` and a mandatory `provenance_url`. - Fetches are SSRF-guarded and bounded by `external_monitor_max_fetch_bytes`; xcrawl scrape (off by default, gated by `XCRAWL_ENABLED` + `XCRAWL_API_KEY`) is the one path that delegates the fetch to an external API. - Suppressed signals are still persisted so audits show the full picture.
